newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan market higher in select demand.
newsitem.headline: Jordan market higher in select demand.

text.p: Jordanian shares firmed for the second day running on Tuesday as local investors bought select industrial shares in bargain-hunting purchases prompted by recent lows, brokers said.

"There were a number of stocks which were attractive buys by local speculators which helped prop the market, but if it is not followed by outside buying or increased liquidity the market could fall again," said Hussam al-Hanbali, a broker in Jordan's Arab Banking Corporation's brokerage arm.
The official Amman Financial Market (AFM) index rose 0.16 percent to 151.60 points, its second day rise after recent falls which sent the bourse on Sunday to its lowest levels in four months.
Brokers say attractively priced stock in some industrials as a result of the recent falls is drawing some local investors back into the market.
However a rebound in prices is dependant on renewed impetus from institutional investors, they add.

Turnover was a low 208,504 dinars ($294,497) dominated by trade in a handful of mostly industrial stock but a half a dinar rise in heavily weighted Arab Bank to 254 dinars, buttressed the official index.
Political uncertainty combined with a lack of liquidity is depressing sentiment and prompting outside buyers and institutional investors to remain on the sidelines.
Only a handful of stock saw much trade, including Intermediate Petrochemicals which rose 0.04 dinars to 0.78 dinars and National Cable and Wire which rose 0.12 dinars to 2.50 dinars in low trade.

Among the busiest stock traded National Portfolio rose 0.03 dinars to 0.97 dinars in low trade worth 24,810 dinars and Jordan Electric Power which gained 0.01 dinars to 1.66 dinars in minimal 13,285 dinars worth of trade.
But reversing a recent trend of across-the-board declines, the market on Tuesday saw 19 shares rising while 13 fell. Another 16 were traded but closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance rose 0.32 percent to 79.57 points, 4.59 percent down from the start of the year.
